title: Colorado's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Colorado's 2nd Congressional District covers north-central Colorado, including Boulder, Fort Collins, Longmont, and numerous rural and mountain communities stretching west along the I-70 corridor. The district has been held by Democrats for over 50 years and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+20, making it the 56th most Democratic district nationally. Incumbent Rep. Joe Neguse (D), first elected in 2018 and serving as House Assistant Democratic Leader, is seeking a fifth term and faces no Democratic primary challenge. Two first-time Republican candidates — Kelley Dennison, a 27-year-old Estes Park massage therapist, and Christina Blunt, a Fort Collins hairstylist — are competing in the June 30 Republican primary for the chance to challenge Neguse in the general election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D' as of February 2025.

candidates.name: Joe Neguse
candidates.summary: Joe Neguse is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 2nd congressional district, first elected in 2018. He serves as House Assistant Democratic Leader, making him the first Coloradan to hold a senior House Democratic leadership position in nearly 90 years, and sits on the Natural Resources, Judiciary, and Rules Committees. Neguse has been recognized as one of the most effective and bipartisan members of Congress by the Center for Effective Lawmaking and the Lugar Center, and he authored the second-highest number of laws of any House member in the 118th Congress.

candidates.name: Kelley Dennison
candidates.summary: Kelley Dennison is a 27-year-old small business owner and licensed massage therapist from Estes Park running for the Republican nomination. She got her start in politics working as a staffer on Adam DeRito's congressional campaign and was inspired to run to give young people a voice. Her campaign priorities include economic affordability, expanding federal funding for trade and vocational education, environmental stewardship, pro-family policies, and Second Amendment rights.

candidates.name: Christina Blunt
candidates.summary: Christina Blunt (Ducommun) is a Fort Collins-based hairstylist and small business owner running for the Republican nomination. A lifelong Republican and petition carrier for Protect Kids Colorado, she entered the race to ensure citizen voices are represented in Congress. Her platform emphasizes fiscal responsibility through a 100% tariff-based revenue system and eliminating the IRS, strong immigration enforcement, cutting regulations to lower costs, and citizen-driven legislation where supporters propose bills.
